title: The 10 Best Airtable Alternatives in 2026: Reviewed and Ranked
summary: Compare 10 leading alternatives by data connections, build speed, governance, deployment, and pricing to find the right fit.
body_markdown:
**If[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/) feels too limiting, too pricey, or too tied to its own system, you have better options in 2026.** I’d narrow the field like this: **[Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/)** is my top pick for teams building on top of existing data, **[Retool](https://docs.retool.com/)** is strong for SQL-heavy internal tools, **[Budibase](https://docs.budibase.com/)** and **[Appsmith](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith)** stand out for self-hosting, **[NocoDB](https://nocodb.com/)** is a simple choice for existing SQL databases, **[Glide](https://app.glide.com/)** is best for spreadsheet-based apps, **Softr** fits portals, **Power Apps** fits Microsoft shops, and **[Quickbase](https://www.quickbase.com/)** fits governance-heavy companies.


I looked at **[10 internal tool builder platforms](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-internal-tool-builder-platforms-in-2026-how-to-choose-the-right-one/)** using **4 buying factors** : **data connections** , **build speed** , **governance and deployment** , and **pricing** . The big pattern is simple: some tools are built for developers, some for business teams, some for spreadsheet users, and some for companies that need tight control over access, hosting, and audit trails.


Here’s the short version:


- **Best overall:** **Jet Admin**
- **Best for SQL databases:** **NocoDB**
- **Best open-source pick:** **Appsmith**
- **Best self-hosted pick:** **[Baserow](https://baserow.io/)**
- **Best spreadsheet-to-app tool:** **Glide**
- **Best for external portals:** **Softr**
- **Best for Microsoft 365 teams:** **[Microsoft Power Apps](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-apps)**
- **Best for large governed workflows:** **Quickbase**
- **Best for developer-led internal tools:** **Retool**
- **Best low-cost open-source option:** **Budibase**


If you’re choosing fast, here’s how I’d think about it:


- Pick **Jet Admin** if you need *many data sources* plus cloud, self-hosted, or on-prem deployment.
- Pick **Retool** if your team is fine with **SQL and JavaScript** .
- Pick **Budibase** or **Appsmith** if you want **open-source** and more hosting control.
- Pick **NocoDB** if you already have **MySQL or PostgreSQL** and want a spreadsheet UI on top.
- Pick **Glide** if your workflow starts in **Google Sheets or Excel** .
- Pick **Softr** if you’re building a **[client portal](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/client-portal-how-to-design-secure-and-launch-a-portal-your-customers-actually-use/) , member area, or light CRM** .
- Pick **Power Apps** if you already pay for and use **Microsoft 365, SharePoint, and Azure** .
- Pick **Quickbase** if admin control matters more than build freedom.

So if I had to sum up the full article in one line, it would be this: **the best Airtable alternative depends less on features alone and more on where your data lives, who is building the app, and how much control you need over hosting, access, and cost.**

## 1.[Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/)


Jet Admin is an AI-powered app builder for teams that want to turn existing data into[internal tools](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/internal-tool-builder) , dashboards, admin panels, and business apps.


### Data-Source Flexibility


Jet Admin connects directly to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB,[Supabase](https://supabase.com/) ,[Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/) , REST APIs, Google Sheets, and Airtable. It also supports cloud storage connections like[Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/) , Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage.


### App-Building Speed


After the data connection is in place, the next step is simple: how fast can a team turn that data into something people can use? Jet Admin comes with **30+ building blocks** and AI-powered relationship detection, which helps speed up database app creation.


That said, it’s not the lightest setup in every case. Some users point to more setup work than simpler no-code tools, and advanced UI customization is more limited than what you’d get with pure code-based builders.


### Governance and Deployment


When a team moves from a test project to production, access control and deployment options start to matter just as much as build speed. Jet Admin supports row-, field-, and API route-level permissions, plus SSO, SAML, audit logs, and built-in authentication with magic link and Google login.


Deployment options include:


- Cloud
- Self-hosted
- On-premise
- Air-gapped environments


### Pricing


Once security and deployment are on the table, pricing becomes less about a public sticker price and more about total cost. Jet Admin offers Cloud, Self-hosted, and On-premise plans by quote.


Because pricing is sales-led, teams should weigh it against their deployment and security needs instead of looking at list price alone.


## 2.[Retool](https://docs.retool.com/)


Retool is a low-code builder made for engineering-led teams that want to ship internal tools on top of existing databases and APIs. It fits best when the people building those tools are comfortable with SQL and JavaScript. That’s the trade-off in plain English: **less simplicity, more control and speed** .


### Data-Source Flexibility


Retool connects to SQL databases, MongoDB, REST and GraphQL APIs, and Google Sheets. Its strongest area is SQL. Relational data lines up cleanly with Retool’s table and form components, which makes common internal-tool workflows feel pretty natural.


That said, Retool works best with relational data. Document data often needs to be flattened before it shows up cleanly in the UI. If your team lives in SQL, that may not feel like a big deal. If you work with messy nested data, it can slow things down.


### App-Building Speed


Retool can get a working CRUD app on screen fast. It comes with more than 100 UI components, including tables, forms, and charts, so teams can assemble internal tools without starting from scratch.


Development also gets a boost from auto-refactoring. When variable names change, Retool updates dependent queries and components for you. In practice, that helps teams ship internal tools much faster than they would with custom code.


The downside is the editor. It’s dense, and because it’s live, accidental clicks during design can trigger real queries or API calls. That can feel a bit like bumping the wrong switch in a busy control room. Native testing is still in closed beta, so many teams lean on external tools instead. For developers, that trade-off may be fine. For nontechnical builders, it’s a tougher sell.


### Governance and Deployment


After an app goes live, the main trade-off shifts to plan limits and access controls. Governance is tied to pricing tiers. Basic roles start on Team, granular RBAC and SSO start on Business, and audit logs plus self-hosting are held for Enterprise.


One thing to watch: Retool does not support automatic key rotation, so teams have to update keys manually.


### Pricing


Pricing looks simple at first, but costs can climb fast as usage grows.


Plan Builder Price End-User Price Deployment Governance


**Team** ~$10/mo ~$5/mo Cloud Basic


**Business** ~$50/mo ~$5/mo Cloud RBAC, SSO


**Enterprise** Custom Custom Cloud or Self-Host Full (Audit Logs, SAML)


Public apps require Business or Enterprise pricing, with a minimum annual commitment of about $600. Per-seat pricing can ramp up fast once a prototype starts spreading across a team or department, so it’s smart to model costs early before locking in.


## 3.[Budibase](https://docs.budibase.com/)


Budibase leans less into heavy developer control and more into **fast open-source app delivery** . Because it’s open-source and self-hostable, it fits teams that want to ship internal apps fast while still keeping more control over where and how those apps run.


### Data-Source Flexibility


Budibase connects internal systems and third-party SaaS tools through a dedicated REST API connector.


### App-Building Speed


Budibase comes with **40+ UI components** and can generate CRUD interfaces from a connected data source in seconds. That can save a lot of setup time, especially when a team needs to move from idea to working app fast.


It’s also known for mobile-ready internal tools and desktop dashboards, which makes it a solid pick for teams that need apps employees can use in the field, not just at a desk. And if the out-of-the-box setup doesn’t cover everything, developers can extend workflows with JavaScript or Python.


### Governance and Deployment


Budibase can be self-hosted on your own infrastructure, with RBAC and SSO available on paid tiers instead of being reserved only for enterprise plans. For teams that care about control but don’t want a long setup slog, that balance matters.


The built-in automation engine includes **20+ triggers and actions** for things like approvals and onboarding.


### Pricing


Cloud plans start as low as **$19/month** . Self-hosting the open-source version is free, while enterprise pricing is custom.


Plan Type Starting Price Deployment


**Free (Open Source)** $0 Self-hosted


**Paid Cloud** As low as $19/month Cloud


**Enterprise** Custom Cloud or Self-hosted


For teams that want open-source freedom without slowing app delivery down, Budibase stands out.


## 4.[Appsmith](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith)


Appsmith is an open-source[low-code platform](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/low-code-app-builder-from-prompt-to-production-ready-business-apps/) built for developers. You get full source-code access and JavaScript support. If your team wants more control than a lighter no-code tool can give, Appsmith is the next step.


### Data-Source Flexibility


Appsmith connects straight to your current databases and APIs, so teams don’t have to move data into a closed system. It works with SQL, NoSQL, and REST/GraphQL APIs, and it comes with **45+ widgets** . That setup makes sense for teams that already have data where they want it and just need a clean app layer on top.


### App-Building Speed


Its drag-and-drop editor uses a **64-column layout grid** , which gives teams tight control over layout and spacing. The flip side? It takes more time to learn than lighter no-code tools, and it offers fewer templates. Teams that are comfortable with JavaScript will usually get more out of it and move faster.


### Governance and Deployment


This is the clearest reason Appsmith ranks here: it gives teams strong control over how apps are built and shipped.


Appsmith includes **Git-based version control** , **Git branch protection** , and **multi-environment support** for development, staging, and production. On the security side, it includes granular RBAC and audit logs. For deployment, teams can choose managed cloud or self-hosting. Self-hosted setups run through Docker or Kubernetes and avoid per-seat fees.


Put simply, Appsmith leans into control, not ease of use.


### Pricing


Plan Starting Price Notes


**Paid Cloud** From $15/user/month User-based pricing


**Usage-Based Cloud** $40/month Includes 100 hours; $0.40/hour after


**Enterprise** Custom SSO, SCIM, dedicated support


Users often point to its deep customization, open-source model, and enterprise security as key reasons to choose it.


## 5.[Baserow](https://baserow.io/)


Baserow is an Airtable-style database platform for teams that want the feel of a spreadsheet without giving up control over how and where their data is managed. It works best for teams that like spreadsheet-style workflows but still want database-level control.


### Data-Source Flexibility


Baserow uses an open-source, API-first setup, which makes it easy to connect with other systems or extend through plugins.


### App-Building Speed


Baserow is fast for turning spreadsheet-style data into apps. But if you need more complex governance or setups with multiple apps, you'll still likely need developer help.


### Governance and Deployment


Baserow supports both managed cloud and self-hosting through Docker or Kubernetes. It also supports RBAC, GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2. More granular permissions and enterprise support are available on paid tiers.


That makes Baserow a good fit for teams that care more about data ownership and deployment control than deep UI customization.


## 6.[NocoDB](https://nocodb.com/)


If your team already stores data in SQL, NocoDB cuts out the migration step. It connects straight to existing databases like **MySQL, PostgreSQL,[SQL Server](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations/microsoft-sql) , and SQLite** and adds a spreadsheet-style interface on top. No data move. No need to rebuild your setup from scratch.


It can also generate a UI from your schema. That makes it a fast pick for teams that already have a database and want to start working from it, instead of setting up a new base first.


NocoDB works well for **internal CRUD apps, views, forms, and simple automations** .


Because NocoDB is open-source, teams keep control over where their data lives. That makes it a strong fit for database-first CRUD apps and internal views.


## 7.[Glide](https://app.glide.com/)


For teams that already run on spreadsheets, **Glide** is one of the fastest ways to turn that data into a[simple internal app](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-internal-tool-builders/) .


It’s built for spreadsheet-first teams, which means you can take data from **Google Sheets** or **Excel** and turn it into an app without much setup. If your team already lives in rows, columns, and tabs, Glide feels like a natural next step.


### Data Source Flexibility


Glide works best for simple apps that sit on top of spreadsheet data. It’s a strong fit for sheet-backed use cases, but it’s not the best pick for[database-heavy workflows](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-no-code-app-builder-how-to-choose-a-platform-that-can-ship-real-business-apps/) or setups with lots of moving parts.


### App-Building Speed


This is where Glide stands out. It’s well known for **fast app creation from Google Sheets** , which makes it a good option when you need to get something live without a long build process.


### Design and Customization


Glide comes with prebuilt templates and components, so you can put together an app fast. The tradeoff is that customization is more limited. If speed matters more than deep workflow control, Glide makes a lot of sense.


That’s why Glide works well for quick spreadsheet-to-app workflows.


## 8. Softr


Softr works well for[client portals](https://www.jetadmin.io/customer-portal) , member directories, and lightweight CRMs. In plain terms, it leans toward customer-facing apps more than back-office admin systems.


### Data Source Flexibility


Softr connects to **21+ data sources** , including Airtable, Google Sheets, Notion,[HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/) , and SQL databases like MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MariaDB, and BigQuery. It also has a native **Softr Databases** layer for built-in storage. On top of that, two-way real-time sync helps keep records up to date across sources.


That setup makes sense for portal-style apps, where data often needs to move between tools people already use, rather than for heavy internal database operations.


### App-Building Speed


Softr puts a lot of focus on speed. Its **AI Co-Builder** can generate the app, schema, pages, and logic from a plain-English prompt in minutes. If you want more control over the interface, the **Vibe Coding** block can generate components and widgets with AI.


Softr also includes **Softr Workflows** for automation triggered by UI actions or data changes. And if you don't want to start from scratch, there are **90+ pre-built templates** available.


### Governance and Deployment


Softr is geared toward external-facing apps. It includes role-based permissions and row-level data restrictions, so users only see the records assigned to them. That's a big deal for client portals, where one user should never peek into another account by accident.


It is **SOC 2 Type II** and **GDPR compliant** , with data hosted in Europe. Apps are mobile-responsive by default and support custom domains and full[white-labeling](https://www.jetadmin.io/audiences/agencies) . **SSO** is available on the Enterprise plan.


Taken together, those controls make Softr a strong option when you need managed external access without a lot of setup.

SQL database integrations start on the **Business** plan, while **Enterprise** adds SSO, dedicated SLAs, and success managers.


## 9.[Microsoft Power Apps](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-apps)


Microsoft Power Apps makes the most sense for teams already running on Microsoft 365, SharePoint, and Azure. In many cases, basic use may already be covered by current licensing. If your company is already deep in the Microsoft stack, Power Apps is usually the most direct option.


### Data Source Flexibility


Power Apps works smoothly with Microsoft-native data sources like SharePoint, Excel, SQL Server, and Dataverse. Dataverse sits at the center of the platform and handles relational data in a way spreadsheet-style tools simply can't.


Power Apps also supports custom connectors and REST APIs for outside systems. That said, there's a catch: premium connectors can push costs up.


### App-Building Speed


Power Apps gives teams two main ways to build:


- *Canvas apps* for drag-and-drop layouts
- *Model-driven apps* for data-first builds


In Microsoft-heavy setups, teams can move fast. But Power Fx, the platform's formula language, is often where things slow down. It has a learning curve that can surprise non-technical users, even though Power Apps is sold as a low-code tool.


### Governance and Deployment


Power Apps uses Azure AD for identity management. It also supports column-level security and row-level filtering through Dataverse.


Deployment follows an environment-based model, with separate development, staging, and production environments using packaged Dataverse solutions. Native CI/CD and Git-based workflows aren't built in, so teams usually need extra tooling to fill that gap. The other issue is licensing: it can get complicated fast.


### Pricing


Pricing is one of the trickier parts of Power Apps. There's a free developer plan for building and testing, but production use requires paid plans priced either per user or per app.


Connector choice also affects cost. Standard connectors are less expensive, while premium connectors add more to the bill. Some Microsoft 365 plans include limited Power Apps use, which can trim costs for current Microsoft customers.


## 10.[Quickbase](https://www.quickbase.com/)


Quickbase is a governed no-code platform built for large teams that need to manage complex business workflows and shared operational data. In plain English: it gives teams one place to manage data tied to projects, tasks, and resourcing instead of letting that information live across scattered tools.


### Data Source Flexibility


Quickbase works best as a governed hub for business data and processes. That setup makes sense for companies that want tighter control over how teams store, use, and share information.


### App-Building Speed


Quickbase uses a WYSIWYG editor and[AI assistant to help teams build structured apps fast](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/no-code-platform-from-ai-prompt-to-production-grade-business-apps/) . That said, it’s a better fit for structured workflows than for teams that want a more open-ended builder with lots of freedom.


### Governance and Deployment


Quickbase puts a lot of weight on admin control and centralized oversight, which is a strong match for teams running complex workflows across many people or departments. If your company cares about guardrails, permissions, and keeping things orderly, that focus will stand out pretty fast.


### Pricing


Quickbase starts at **$35/user/month** when billed annually, and it comes with a **30-day free trial** . It’s priced for enterprise use, and its focus on structured workflows can feel limiting for teams with broader needs. Those trade-offs are easier to see in the comparison below.

## FAQs


### How do I choose the right Airtable alternative for my team?


Choose based on your team’s technical skills, data needs, and governance requirements. Start by pinning down the main use case, whether that’s project management or building secure internal tools on top of existing databases.


Then compare candidates on a few key points:


- data connectivity
- governance features like SSO, audit logs, and row-level permissions
- builder skill level
- deployment options


Before you make the call, run a **2-to-4-week pilot** with one real workflow.


### Which tools work best with existing SQL databases?


Several platforms work well with existing SQL databases, so you can build internal tools **without moving your data** .


**Jet Admin** connects to PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and other databases as a frontend and logic layer. **NocoDB** adds a spreadsheet-style interface. And tools like **Retool** , **Appsmith** , **Softr** , and **Budibase** support SQL-based dashboards, CRUD apps, and internal tools.


### Which option is best for self-hosting and compliance?


For teams that put self-hosting and compliance first, the top picks are the ones that support on-premise or private cloud deployment. That matters for **data residency** and **network isolation** , especially when sensitive data can't leave your setup.


**Baserow** is a strong match for teams dealing with **GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2** requirements. **Appsmith** , **[ToolJet](https://www.tooljet.com/)** , and **Budibase** give you full self-hosted control. **[DronaHQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DronaHQ)** and **Jet Admin** add enterprise-grade security features, including **audit logs** and **granular access controls** .
